sentences.text: After due execution of necessary documents, the plaintiff released the aforesaid payment under the said agreement vide consolidated cheque no.014772 dated 09.02.2018 drawn on City Union Bank, in favour of "ARC Motors Pvt. Ltd." and the defendant received the above said product from the dealer.
Further, it is averred that the payment schedule under the said agreement was on the basis of monthly installment of Rs.2505 x 24 from 20.04.2018 to 20.03.2020.
Defendant no.1 failed to pay even one EMI.

It is averred that as on 12.11.2019 the defendants are liable to pay the following amount alongwith interest: Payment starting date 20.04.2018 Closing date 20.03.2020 Scheme (Rs. 2505 X 24 months including interest) Rs.60,120/

Payment received Nil Balance due Rs.59,073/ Delay Penalty up till 17.10.2019 as overdue Rs.12,669/ Cheque returning charges 18 cheques Rs.10,620/ Total Rs.82,362/ Despite various requests and reminders defendants failed to clear the outstanding amount/ installments, therefore, plaintiff sent a legal notice dated 12.11.2019 through speed post on 14.11.2019 to the defendant for recovery of outstanding amount of Rs.82,362/ but of no avail.
Hence, the present suit.

sentences.text: The plaint otherwise, as per the amended CPC, besides being verified, is also supported by a affidavit of the plaintiff.

I failed to fathom any reason for according any additional sanctity to the affidavit by way of examination in chief then to the affidavit in support of the plaint or to any exhibit mark being put on the documents which have been filed by the plaintiff and are already on record.
I have therefore, heard the counsel for the plaintiff on merits qua relief of injunction...."

7. The onus to establish its case rested on plaintiff.

The plaintiff has relied upon original loan Hypothecation Agreement, copy of bank statement, original invoice, account statements maintained by the plaintiff against the account of defendant and legal notice dated 12.11.2019 to prove its case.
8. The suit has been filed on 11.03.2020 which is within the prescribed period of limitation.

It is submitted that Loan Hypothecation Agreement between the plaintiff and defendants was executed at the head office of plaintiff in Delhi, hence, this court has territorial jurisdiction to pass the decree against the defendant.
9.
The plaintiff has also claimed delay penalty/ interest at the rate of 5% per moth amounting to Rs.12,669/ and cheque returning charges of Rs.10,620/.

As per Section 74 of Indian Contract Act 1872, where, the contract contains stipulation by way of penalty, the party complaining of the breach is entitled to receive from the party who has broken the contract a reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount so named or the penalty stipulated for.

In the present case, claim of interest @ 5 % per month is certainly excessive and as the name of interest (Delay Penalty) suggests, the same is in the form of Penalty which is not permissible U/s 74 of Indian Contract Act.
